# Original 2014 Cicada Freenode log corpus: recovered public source locator

**Agent40, 14 November 2026. Independently recovered period-origin community record, not a Cicada-authored cipher instruction.** The previous research frontier treated the original May–August 2014 `#cicadasolvers` Freenode transcripts as absent. An existing public fork of the original `neuroretransmit/cicada` archive contains two full `#cicadasolvers` channel logs, with **236,650 timestamped 2014 lines in the first file**, and an additional 38,008 from September–December in the second. A separate `#33012014` channel file has a further 110,607 timestamped 2014 lines. All three original files were fully retrieved and verified byte-for-byte against original Git blob identifiers on GitHub Actions. The exact original chat records are accessible as complete Git objects, with timestamps and participant-attributed text; they are not an interpretation assembled from modern walkthroughs.

## Original source file identities and coverage

The public source is [the preserved IRC log directory](https://github.com/cicada-solvers/neuroretransmit-cicada/tree/main/irc-logs), retaining filenames of the older original `neuroretransmit/cicada` tree. The three pinned original source objects are:

| Original source path | Bytes | Git blob SHA1 | Date coverage |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| [`#cicadasolvers.freenode.log`](https://github.com/cicada-solvers/neuroretransmit-cicada/blob/main/irc-logs/%23cicadasolvers.freenode.log) | 18,487,233 | `bdd277c14f94c34b5ae714cd00c238065beeed4e` | January–September 2014, 236,650 dated lines |
| [`#cicadasolvers.freenode.2.log`](https://github.com/cicada-solvers/neuroretransmit-cicada/blob/main/irc-logs/%23cicadasolvers.freenode.2.log) | 27,234,234 | `72634a9d071d32af767edbffc0493d810e88cd0d` | September–December 2014: 38,008 dated lines; also 2015–16 |
| [`#33012014.freenode.log`](https://github.com/cicada-solvers/neuroretransmit-cicada/blob/main/irc-logs/%2333012014.freenode.log) | 8,629,610 | `a2880b1db31ce523599ef30ca2e55291bf295900` | January–August 2014, 110,607 dated lines |

The full `#cicadasolvers` first-file 2014 monthly counts (source text lines prefixed `2014 Mon DD HH:MM`) are **Jan 94,818; Feb 43,172; Mar 15,101; Apr 8,901; May 29,249; Jun 23,228; Jul 13,836; Aug 8,235; Sep 110**. This proves **74,548 directly dated May–August 2014 channel lines** in the original primary channel file. The separate #33012014 source adds another **2,091** dated May–August 2014 lines. Exact original timestamps are recorded with minute resolution; these are date-bearing text exports and not cryptographic proof of the identities behind nicknames.

Some May–August original channel posts specifically mention `http://titanpad.com/vFCy7T5p0O` and a separate transcription pad `http://titanpad.com/hJ8pVQ5S43`. On **19 August 2014 23:56**, `#cicadasolvers` has a line stating that someone asked about the page-56 hash on StackExchange. These are historical participant observations, not a solved preimage or an original author response. The source also contains IRC messages under nickname `cluosh` before and during 2014, the name credited with the original p56 solution; no independent identity attestation follows from the nickname. **First historical p56 solve, 19 May 2014, recovered in the original log.** The primary channel supplies a complete first-person sequence under the IRC nickname `cluosh`:
- **01:55–01:56, source L180878–87:** mentions the prime sequence from the May-2 upload, explicitly includes missing **19**, and announces `AN END: WITHIN` for page 56.
- **01:58, L180896–906:** identifies primes modulo 29 as GP29 shifting values, extending plaintext to `AN END: WITHIN THE`.
- **02:09–02:18, L180931–64:** rejects a mistakenly inferred 19-symbol repeating key, publishes consecutive prime-minus-one residues (`1-2-4-6-10-12-16-18-22-28...`) and specifies `ciphertext - key = clear`.
- **02:30–02:35, L181015–48:** another participant (`mdzhb`) prints the complete non-hash English message and identifies the book's first successful page solve.
- **02:51–03:01, L181096–131:** `cluosh` says `AN END` was already a guessed plaintext crib; the group identifies the unencrypted plaintext `F` and the no-key-advance rule.
- **21 May, L184921–28:** `cluosh` says that guessing the first two words enabled the prime interpretation, acknowledges possible luck, and explains that the Euler-totient description came later.

This clarifies the May-15 `totient` question (L178827) immediately followed by `jk` (L178828), which **does not** date a successful solve; June-19 L205898/L206244 are much later retellings. The original upload's visible whitespace run counts 2,3,5,7,11,13,17,23,29,31,37 fit the reported missing-19 prime sequence, **but ten of those runs are not signed** and archived copies differ at 7/23 versus 6/22. Thus the IRC evidence establishes the human solver's selection path without authenticating the upload's incidental bytes as a reusable LP2 key. This source first-method extraction was verified against all original log blobs in [successful CI 43603578484](https://github.com/FlareZ123/liber-primus/actions/runs/43603578484), using [the CommonJS exact-byte SFT](../../sims/lp2_2014_p56_method_origin_sft.cjs). p56 complete authenticity is separately verified in [the existing regression](../../im-results/authentic-decryption-regression.md). The direct 11-value upload prime reuse on p0 already failed in [the bounded original-cipher test](../../im-results/historical-may2-whitespace-source-gate.md); no unknown-page plaintext is inferred.

**2014 unknown-page crib witness screen:** A second source-identical, cross-message [dialogue and key-claim screen](../../sims/lp2_2014_irc_inchannel_dialogue_sft.cjs) found a **23 May 2014 L186651** speculation that p54 starts `A Beginning`, explicitly qualified `beginning doesn't fit`; this predates the archived May **2016** Titanpad iteration of that crib. The same original dialogue gives a **16 May 2014 L179463–64** participant-suggested formula `M(n)=abs(3301-P(F(n)+1))`. This is **exactly the known generator of the original p15 Fibonacci-prime 4×4 square**, reproducing all 16 cells under the unique-Fibonacci clockwise center-out order ([existing exact artifact SFT](../../sims/fibonacci_prime_spiral.cjs)). It is a source-dated recognition of an authentic printed-math operation, **without a specified ciphertext-to-plaintext GP29 inverse, unknown-page plaintext or key**. [Original-byte Windows CI 43611424980](https://github.com/FlareZ123/liber-primus/actions/runs/43611424980).  The same first-party source record also preserves hypothetical non-p56 plaintext guesses on May21 p25 (`CONDITIONEDNESS`), May24 p35 (`IT'S` with shifts 26–28) and p34 (`LESS` with shifts 27,28,0,1), and May27 p11 (`OVERSIMPLIFYING`). These are explicitly tentative guesses and the original phase progression **fails immediately** on the untouched next p34 and p35 printed words (`EFE` and `JSDD`). The 2014 participants had no reproducible broader page solution in those captured contexts. [Source-pinned full witness screen and original-rune holdout](../../im-results/lp2-2014-original-irc-unknown-page-crib-holdout.md) · [successful CI run 43606051226](https://github.com/FlareZ123/liber-primus/actions/runs/43606051226).

## Reproduction and research significance

[The original-byte CommonJS SFT](../../sims/lp2_2014_original_irc_log_source_gate_sft.cjs) checks every Git blob SHA1 and exact original byte count before computing per-year/per-month tallies and extracting source-line numbers for p56/hash/totality clues. [Successful original-source GitHub Actions run 43599552893](https://github.com/FlareZ123/liber-primus/actions/runs/43599552893) recovered all three complete files, verified them, and printed source line numbers and counts. Existing earlier [May-2014-pad archival research](../../im-results/lp2-2014-may-unfiction-workpad-source-gate.md) had found only April–July **2016** snapshots and no 2014 chat; the present original IRC discovery materially resolves that historical acquisition gap, independently of recovering any original target URL.

This public source may enable historically grounded testing of when p56 was first decoded, which keys were proposed, and whether anyone recorded the unidentified continuation URL. It must be inspected for actual messages before crediting any claim. Nicknames, channel URLs, participant guesses and records from `#33012014` should remain distinct from signed Cicada instructions. **No unsolved original LP2 plaintext, matching p56 digest preimage, or historical intended key has been recovered by this discovery alone.**
